clue.text: Regret shown about small daughter being discourteous

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the word for regret surrounds the daughter

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it
D is the standard short form of daughter, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone sorry about how they treated a young girl has been impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: A rude person is impolite and lacking in manners.

clue.text: A put-down say in a story

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for say inside the story

parts.note: a relation is a narrative or account
eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: An example of humiliation inside a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put-down' looks like an insult; here it is a demotion, as in a team dropping a division.
explanation.definitionFit: Relegation is being moved down to a lower rank or division.

clue.text: Raise an objection which is almost modest

indicators.note: almost means the word for modest is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: demure means modest and reserved

explanation.surface: Protesting in a nearly shy way.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to voice a doubt or objection.

clue.text: Out of place, as the underworld found

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for the underworld itself
to have located something is to have found it

explanation.surface: Something displaced, as discovered by gangland figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The underworld' suggests criminals, but here it is DIS, the classical realm of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A dislocated joint or object has been knocked out of its proper position.

clue.text: The person feeling no obligation to take in some bars

parts.note: taken as written
a grate is a framework of metal bars

explanation.surface: Someone who owes no thanks agrees to pop into a few pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests pubs, but it is the iron bars of a grate.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person who feels no debt for kindness received.

clue.text: Means of bearing youngsters!

definitions.meaning: stretchers or covered couches on which people were carried
broods of young animals born together

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses carry the idea of bearing: one carries people, the other is what an animal bears.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter is both a carried couch or stretcher and a set of animal offspring born at one time.

clue.text: Amusing yet firm male in charge

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
IC means in charge, as in second-in-command

explanation.surface: A funny but strict man running things.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic means funny or causing laughter.

clue.text: Fury consumed the moderate

parts.note: temper means a fit of anger or fury
ate means consumed food

explanation.surface: Rage devoured the middle-of-the-road politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate means restrained and avoiding extremes.

clue.text: Sort of timber to treat

definitions.meaning: softwood planks, from pine or fir
to handle or cope with a matter

explanation.definitionFit: Deal is pine or fir wood, and to deal with something is to handle or tackle it.

clue.text: Tidy up box filled with audio equipment

indicators.note: filled with puts the hearing organ inside the word for box

parts.note: to box is to hit, and a clout is a blow
the ear is the body's equipment for hearing

explanation.surface: Sorting out a carton packed with hi-fi gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container; it is a punch, CLOUT, and 'audio equipment' is the ear, not a stereo.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear-out is a session of tidying, getting rid of unwanted things.

clue.text: Spot fruit that is underweight

parts.note: a lime is a green citrus fruit
something light weighs less than it should, like a short measure

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit is found to be short of its stated weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' is the definition, as in a spotlight: the limelight was the stage lamp of the old theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A limelight was a theatre spotlight, and being in the limelight means being in the public glare.

clue.text: Ophidian scholar followed by many another

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate scholar
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
another scholar is a BA, Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A snake expert is followed around by lots of other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another scholar, so a second degree, BA.
explanation.definitionFit: An ophidian is any snake, and the mamba is a venomous African snake.

clue.text: A drawback for the Irish police

indicators.note: back says the letters of a draw are to be read in the other direction

parts.note: to drag is to draw or pull along

explanation.surface: A disadvantage for the police force in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawback' splits into 'draw' (DRAG) and 'back', which turns A DRAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garda Síochána is the national police service of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Middle-men a long time since perhaps

parts.note: an age is a very long period

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of since could be put in another order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether brokers have been around for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Agencies act as intermediaries, arranging business between two other parties.

clue.text: A businessman's swindle over agricultural machinery

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the swindle above the farm vehicle

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A business type cheats a farmer over a tractor.
explanation.definitionFit: A contractor is a self-employed person or firm hired to carry out work.

clue.text: Got up after a cuppa such a bloomer!

indicators.note: after places the word for got up following the drink

parts.note: a cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea
rose means got up out of bed

explanation.surface: Someone rose after their morning tea and made a dreadful blunder!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea rose is a hybrid garden rose, a plant that blooms, with a scent likened to tea.

clue.text: Transport for patients and medico involved in a universal cut

indicators.note: involved in means the doctor's degree is put inside the following letters

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing
to lance is to cut open with a blade
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor joins a general pay cut, affecting patient transport.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance is a vehicle that carries the sick or injured to hospital.

clue.text: She's invariably scored highly

parts.note: reads like a woman who always gets high marks, but describes a singer whose part is always written in the highest register of a score

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' means written in a musical score, not given marks.
explanation.definitionFit: The soprano is the highest female voice, so her music is always written high on the stave.

clue.text: Keep a rat, maybe, or a bird

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of keep a rat can be rearranged

explanation.surface: Choosing between owning a rodent or a feathered pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small long-tailed parrot.

clue.text: Going round to take part in viva voce examination

indicators.note: in puts the word for part inside the examination

parts.note: an oral is an exam conducted by speaking, viva voce
a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: Travelling round the circuit to sit part of a spoken examination.
explanation.definitionFit: Something orbital follows a circular path, like a satellite or a ring road.

clue.text: Reluctant trendy accepting a place in Scotland

parts.note: loth means unwilling or reluctant

indicators.note: accepting means the fashionable word takes the letter a inside it

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: An unwilling hipster agreeing to a spot north of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothian is a region of south-east Scotland around Edinburgh.

clue.text: Left about ten — a bad sign indeed!

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for left goes around the number

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship
taken as written

explanation.surface: Departing at around ten o'clock is an ominous omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like departed, but it is PORT, the nautical left side.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is an omen, usually one foreshadowing something calamitous.

clue.text: A lady's note repeatedly appearing in the newspapers

indicators.note: appearing in places the repeated note inside the newspapers

parts.note: the press means newspapers collectively

indicators.note: repeatedly means the musical note is written twice

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A woman's message keeps turning up in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a message; it is the musical note E, given twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeress is a woman holding a title of nobility, such as a duchess or countess.

clue.text: Making money in a great deal, support a man with a portion

indicators.note: in places the money symbol inside the phrase for a great deal

parts.note: a lot means a great deal
L is the abbreviation for pound, the British currency unit, from Latin libra
a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Earning money in a big transaction, backing someone with a share.
explanation.definitionFit: An allottee is a person to whom a share or allocation has been given.

clue.text: Had done badly — without a single point

indicators.note: without means outside, so the rearranged letters surround the compass point
badly suggests the letters of done are jumbled

parts.note: W, west, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: Performed poorly and failed to score a single point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here: 'badly' turns DONE into ONED, which goes round W.
explanation.definitionFit: Owned means possessed, which is what had means in the sense of having something.

clue.text: The Greek character always in silk apparel

indicators.note: in signals the letters are tucked inside the words silk apparel

explanation.surface: A Greek person who always dresses in silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Kappa is the tenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: A really big river vessel

definitions.meaning: the River ..., the vast estuary between Argentina and Uruguay

explanation.walkthrough: 'River vessel' suggests a boat, but the river and the vessel are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The River Plate is a huge South American estuary, and a plate is a flat dish.

clue.text: Gets very chilly in even the nicest weather

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the word nicest

explanation.surface: Turning cold even in the finest weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice is to freeze over or become icy cold.

clue.text: Order article to go in study

indicators.note: to go in places the article inside the word for study

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Instruction for a piece of furniture to be put in the den.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for study is an old sense, as in conning one's lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a rule or decree, especially one laid down by a church.

clue.text: New line offered by cunning agent lacking polish

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of line are made into something fresh
cunning suggests the letters of agent are slyly rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh story put forward by a crafty spy lacks finesse.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: 'New' rearranges LINE into INEL and 'cunning' rearranges AGENT into EGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inelegant is clumsy and lacks grace or refinement.

clue.text: Drink and eats must be loaded into a ship when it's calm

indicators.note: loaded into means the drink and food are put inside the ship like cargo

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
tea is a drink
to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Provisions of tea and food are stowed aboard a vessel in calm weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadiness is a settled, unshaken state, the absence of agitation.

clue.text: Concerned with a right back

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Something about a right-back in football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right back' looks like a football defender; split it, R for right and 'back' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear is the back part of something.
